newsitem.title: USA: Lawmaker vows to work with Clinton on fast track.
newsitem.headline: Lawmaker vows to work with Clinton on fast track.

text.p: House Ways and Means trade subcommittee Chairman Phil Crane said on Thursday he was committed to working with President Clinton on providing fast track trade negotiating authority.

"This authority, which is delegated from Congress, is essential for the president to have if American businesses, consumers and workers are to benefit from growing opportunities in international markets, Crane, an Illinois Republican, said in a statement.

Fast track authority, which would allow the administration to negotiate trade agreements with other countries without fear they will be later changed by Congress, is one of a number of trade initiatives outlined by the president in his proposed 1998 budget.

Clinton also proposed extending authorization for the Generalized System of Preferences (GSP), which allows certain goods from developing countries to be imported duty free. The current program expires on May 31.

The president also proposed giving eligible countries of the Caribbean Basin Initiative the same access to U.S. markets for certain goods as given Mexico under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).
Crane said he supported reauthorization of GSP and was "heartened" by Clinton's Caribbean Basin proposal.

"This effort is urgently needed in order to address the unintended effect of the (NAFTA) which has been to divert needed foreign investment from Caribbean and Central American countries to Mexico," Crane said.
